concepts.definition: Scope defined strictly at author time by the physical placement of blocks in code.
The internal dictionary data structure that maps variable names to values inside an Execution Context.
The internal store that holds legacy function-scoped `var` variables.
The internal store that holds modern block-scoped `let`, `const`, and `class` variables.
An observational artifact of the Creation Phase allocating memory for identifiers before code runs.
The time interval between scope entry and declaration line evaluation where accessing a variable throws a `ReferenceError`.

concepts.definition: A function bundled with references to its enclosing Lexical Environment (`[[Scopes]]`).
The compiler phase where V8 determines whether a local variable escapes the Call Stack and must be allocated on the heap.
The internal, hidden property on every JS function object that points to its parent lexical contexts.
A watch list array passed as the second argument to `useEffect` telling React when to re-execute the effect.
A closure that holds onto an outdated execution context snapshot while the surrounding application has moved forward to newer state.
A V8 memory leak where an unused large variable is kept alive because another active closure shares the same lexical `Context` object.
